name: eng-2267

cases.title: The search toolbar uses Obsidian's UI font size

steps.why: open node search the way a user would

cases.proves: Done When 1: The modal's toolbar/dropdown components render with correct pixel parity and scale with Obsidian's font-size setting.
cases.caption: Node search's toolbar now takes its sizes from Obsidian's own variables, so the query field and its triggers match Obsidian's menus.

expect.js: (() => { const field = document.querySelector('.modal [role="textbox"]'); proof.assert(field, 'No search field in the modal.'); const want = getComputedStyle(document.body).getPropertyValue('--font-ui-medium').trim(); proof.assert(want && getComputedStyle(field.parentElement).fontSize === want, 'The search field is ' + getComputedStyle(field.parentElement).fontSize + ', not --font-ui-medium (' + want + ').'); })()

cases.title: The filter panel draws its border and dividers
cases.proves: Done When 1: The modal's toolbar/dropdown components render with correct pixel parity and scale with Obsidian's font-size setting.
cases.caption: The filter panel now draws its border and dividers, which never rendered before.

expect.js: (() => { const panel = document.querySelector('.modal div.absolute.top-full'); proof.assert(panel, 'The filter panel is not open.'); const style = getComputedStyle(panel); proof.assert(style.borderTopStyle === 'solid' && parseFloat(style.borderTopWidth) > 0, 'The filter panel has no border.'); const divider = panel.querySelector('.border-b'); proof.assert(!divider || getComputedStyle(divider).borderBottomStyle === 'solid', 'A filter panel divider has no border.'); })()

cases.title: The sort panel matches Obsidian's menus too
cases.proves: Done When 1: The modal's toolbar/dropdown components render with correct pixel parity and scale with Obsidian's font-size setting.
cases.caption: The sort panel gets the same border and spacing.

expect.js: (() => { const panel = document.querySelector('.modal div.absolute.top-full'); proof.assert(panel, 'The sort panel is not open.'); const style = getComputedStyle(panel); proof.assert(style.borderTopStyle === 'solid' && parseFloat(style.borderTopWidth) > 0, 'The sort panel has no border.'); })()

cases.title: Search dialog fits with default theme

steps.why: open node search the way a user would

cases.intent: In Obsidian with the default theme, open the node search dialog from the command palette. Look at the input, the filter button and the sort button in the top row.

expect.js: (() => { const probe = (prop, v) => { const e = document.createElement('div'); e.style[prop] = 'var(' + v + ')'; document.body.appendChild(e); const out = getComputedStyle(e)[prop]; e.remove(); return out; }; const px = (n) => parseFloat(n); const near = (a, b) => Math.abs(a - b) <= 1; const box = document.querySelector('.modal [role="textbox"]')?.parentElement; const filter = document.querySelector('.modal button[title="Filter by type"]'); const sort = document.querySelector('.modal button[title^="Sort by"]'); proof.assert(box && filter && sort, 'The search field, filter button or sort button is missing.'); const row = box.parentElement; const modal = row.closest('.modal').getBoundingClientRect(); const b = box.getBoundingClientRect(); const f = filter.parentElement.getBoundingClientRect(); const s = sort.parentElement.getBoundingClientRect(); for (const r of [f, s]) proof.assert(r.top < b.bottom && r.bottom > b.top, 'A trigger is not on the field row.'); const want = px(probe('paddingLeft', '--size-4-2')); proof.assert(near(f.left - b.right, want) && near(s.left - f.right, want), 'The gaps are ' + (f.left - b.right) + 'px and ' + (s.left - f.right) + 'px, not --size-4-2 (' + want + 'px).'); proof.assert(near(px(getComputedStyle(row).paddingLeft), px(probe('paddingLeft', '--size-4-1'))), 'The row padding is not --size-4-1.'); for (const r of [b, f, s]) proof.assert(r.left >= modal.left && r.right <= modal.right && r.top >= modal.top && r.bottom <= modal.bottom, 'Part of the toolbar sits outside the dialog.'); })()

cases.checks: The field and both triggers share one row, are spaced by --size-4-2, and nothing sticks out of the dialog.

cases.title: Chips wrap inline with query text

steps.why: open node search the way a user would
type the start of a node type
Tab turns it into a chip

type.text: a long query that keeps going so the search field has to wrap onto a second line of text inside the box, and then a bit more to be sure it does

steps.why: type a long query so the field wraps
click the first chip to focus it

cases.intent: Type a node type prefix and press Tab to make it a chip. Add several chips and a long query so the field wraps to two lines. Click a chip to focus it.

expect.js: (() => { const probe = (prop, v) => { const e = document.createElement('div'); e.style[prop] = 'var(' + v + ')'; document.body.appendChild(e); const out = getComputedStyle(e)[prop]; e.remove(); return out; }; const px = (n) => parseFloat(n); const near = (a, b) => Math.abs(a - b) <= 1; const field = document.querySelector('.modal [role="textbox"]'); const box = field.parentElement; const chips = [...box.querySelectorAll('span[role="button"][aria-label^="PK 2267"]')]; proof.assert(chips.length === 3, 'Expected 3 chips, found ' + chips.length + '.'); const style = getComputedStyle(field); const line = px(style.lineHeight) || px(style.fontSize) * 1.3; const bb = box.getBoundingClientRect(); proof.assert(bb.height >= 2 * line, 'The field did not wrap: it is ' + bb.height + 'px tall for lines of ' + line + 'px.'); for (const chip of chips) { const r = chip.getBoundingClientRect(); proof.assert(r.left >= bb.left && r.right <= bb.right && r.top >= bb.top && r.bottom <= bb.bottom, 'A chip sits outside the field.'); } const cs = getComputedStyle(chips[0]); proof.assert(near(px(cs.marginRight), px(probe('paddingLeft', '--size-4-1'))) && near(px(cs.paddingLeft), px(probe('paddingLeft', '--size-4-2'))), 'The chip margin or padding is off the --size-4-* tokens.'); proof.assert(cs.fontSize === probe('fontSize', '--font-ui-smaller'), 'The chip text is not --font-ui-smaller.'); proof.assert(cs.outlineStyle === 'solid' && px(cs.outlineWidth) > 0, 'The focused chip has no outline.'); })()

cases.checks: Three chips and the long query wrap inside the field, the chips use the size tokens, and the clicked chip shows its focus outline.

cases.title: Tab completion hint spacing

steps.why: open node search the way a user would
type part of a node type name

do.js: (() => { const probe = (prop, v) => { const e = document.createElement('div'); e.style[prop] = 'var(' + v + ')'; document.body.appendChild(e); const out = getComputedStyle(e)[prop]; e.remove(); return out; }; const px = (n) => parseFloat(n); const near = (a, b) => Math.abs(a - b) <= 1; const kbd = document.querySelector('.modal [role="textbox"] ~ span kbd'); proof.assert(kbd, 'No Tab hint.'); const suffix = kbd.previousElementSibling; proof.assert(suffix && suffix.textContent.endsWith('pha'), 'The grey suffix is "' + (suffix && suffix.textContent) + '", not the rest of Alpha.'); proof.assert(near(px(getComputedStyle(kbd).marginLeft), px(probe('paddingLeft', '--size-4-2'))), 'The hint is not --size-4-2 from the suffix.'); })()

steps.why: check the suffix and the hint spacing

cases.intent: Type a partial node type name so the grey completion suffix and the Tab key hint show. Then press Tab.

expect.js: (() => { const field = document.querySelector('.modal [role="textbox"]'); proof.assert(document.querySelector('.modal span[role="button"][aria-label="PK 2267 Alpha"]'), 'Tab did not make a PK 2267 Alpha chip.'); proof.assert(!field.textContent.trim(), 'The query was not cleared.'); proof.assert(!document.querySelector('.modal [role="textbox"] ~ span kbd'), 'The hint is still showing.'); })()

cases.checks: The hint sits --size-4-2 after the grey suffix, and Tab turns the name into a chip and clears the field.

cases.title: Count badge on the filter trigger

steps.why: open node search the way a user would

do.js: (() => { const probe = (prop, v) => { const e = document.createElement('div'); e.style[prop] = 'var(' + v + ')'; document.body.appendChild(e); const out = getComputedStyle(e)[prop]; e.remove(); return out; }; const px = (n) => parseFloat(n); const near = (a, b) => Math.abs(a - b) <= 1; const button = document.querySelector('.modal button[title="Filter by type"]'); const badge = button.querySelector(':scope > span[aria-hidden]'); proof.assert(badge && badge.textContent.trim() === '2', 'The badge does not show 2.'); const b = badge.getBoundingClientRect(); const t = button.getBoundingClientRect(); const off = px(probe('paddingLeft', '--size-4-1')); proof.assert(near(b.right - t.right, off) && near(t.top - b.top, off), 'The badge is offset ' + (b.right - t.right) + 'px and ' + (t.top - b.top) + 'px, not --size-4-1 (' + off + 'px).'); const cs = getComputedStyle(badge); proof.assert(cs.fontSize === probe('fontSize', '--font-ui-smaller') && cs.borderTopLeftRadius === probe('borderTopLeftRadius', '--radius-m'), 'The badge font size or radius is off the tokens.'); })()

cases.title: Filter panel Clear filter and type search

steps.why: open node search the way a user would
wait for the Clear filter strip

do.js: (() => { const probe = (prop, v) => { const e = document.createElement('div'); e.style[prop] = 'var(' + v + ')'; document.body.appendChild(e); const out = getComputedStyle(e)[prop]; e.remove(); return out; }; const px = (n) => parseFloat(n); const near = (a, b) => Math.abs(a - b) <= 1; const panel = document.querySelector('.modal div.absolute.top-full'); const strip = [...panel.querySelectorAll('div')].find((d) => d.querySelector(':scope > button') && /Clear filter/.test(d.textContent)); proof.assert(strip, 'No Clear filter strip.'); const cs = getComputedStyle(strip); proof.assert(cs.borderBottomStyle === 'solid' && px(cs.borderBottomWidth) > 0, 'The strip has no divider.'); proof.assert(near(px(cs.paddingLeft), px(probe('paddingLeft', '--size-4-2'))), 'The strip padding is off --size-4-2.'); const search = panel.querySelector('input[type="text"]'); proof.assert(search, 'No type search above seven types.'); proof.assert(getComputedStyle(search.parentElement).borderBottomStyle === 'solid', 'The type search has no divider.'); })()

steps.why: check the strip and search dividers
type nonsense into the type search

do.js: (() => { const probe = (prop, v) => { const e = document.createElement('div'); e.style[prop] = 'var(' + v + ')'; document.body.appendChild(e); const out = getComputedStyle(e)[prop]; e.remove(); return out; }; const px = (n) => parseFloat(n); const near = (a, b) => Math.abs(a - b) <= 1; const empty = document.querySelector('.modal div.absolute.top-full div.text-center'); proof.assert(/No matching node types/.test(empty.textContent), 'The empty state text is wrong.'); const cs = getComputedStyle(empty); proof.assert(cs.fontSize === probe('fontSize', '--font-ui-small') && near(px(cs.paddingLeft), px(probe('paddingLeft', '--size-4-4'))), 'The empty state is off the tokens.'); })()

cases.intent: With many node types configured, open the filter panel. Tick one type and confirm the Clear filter strip appears. Type nonsense into the type search box. Then click Clear filter.

expect.js: (() => { const panel = document.querySelector('.modal div.absolute.top-full'); proof.assert(panel, 'The panel closed.'); proof.assert(!/Clear filter/.test(panel.textContent), 'The Clear filter strip is still there.'); proof.assert(getComputedStyle(panel.querySelector('input[type="text"]').parentElement).borderBottomStyle === 'solid', 'The type search lost its divider.'); })()

expect.js: (() => { const probe = (prop, v) => { const e = document.createElement('div'); e.style[prop] = 'var(' + v + ')'; document.body.appendChild(e); const out = getComputedStyle(e)[prop]; e.remove(); return out; }; const px = (n) => parseFloat(n); const near = (a, b) => Math.abs(a - b) <= 1; const panel = document.querySelector('.modal div.absolute.top-full'); proof.assert(panel, 'The sort menu closed.'); const checked = panel.querySelector('[role="menuitemradio"][aria-checked="true"]'); proof.assert(checked && /Date created/.test(checked.textContent), 'Date created is not the selected option.'); const pressed = panel.querySelector('div[role="button"][aria-pressed="true"]'); proof.assert(pressed, 'No direction is pressed.'); const button = document.querySelector('.modal button[title^="Sort by"]'); proof.assert(button.title !== window.__dg2267SortTitle && button.title.endsWith(pressed.title), 'The direction toggle did not change the sort.'); const toggle = pressed.parentElement; const cs = getComputedStyle(toggle); proof.assert(cs.borderTopStyle === 'solid' && px(cs.borderTopWidth) > 0, 'The direction toggle has no top border.'); proof.assert(near(px(cs.paddingLeft), px(probe('paddingLeft', '--size-4-2'))) && getComputedStyle(pressed).borderTopLeftRadius === probe('borderTopLeftRadius', '--radius-s'), 'The direction toggle is off the tokens.'); })()

cases.title: Change Appearance font size

do.js: (async () => { const app = window.app; if (typeof app.updateFontSize !== 'function' || typeof app.vault.getConfig !== 'function' || typeof app.vault.setConfig !== 'function') throw new Error('This Obsidian has no vault.getConfig/setConfig or app.updateFontSize, so the font size cannot be changed from here.'); await proof.obsidian.closeModals(); const orig = app.vault.getConfig('baseFontSize'); window.__dg2267FontSize = typeof orig === 'number' ? orig : 16; const rootBefore = parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).fontSize); window.__dg2267UiSmall = getComputedStyle(document.body).getPropertyValue('--font-ui-small').trim(); const next = window.__dg2267FontSize >= 20 ? 12 : 22; app.vault.setConfig('baseFontSize', next); app.updateFontSize(); await proof.waitFor(() => parseFloat(getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).fontSize) !== rootBefore, { what: 'the Appearance font size to take effect', timeout: 5000 }); return next; })()

title: Native-Obsidian styling pass for advanced node search
claim: Advanced node search's toolbar and its filter and sort panels take their sizes, spacing and corners from Obsidian's own variables, and the panels draw the border they were always meant to.
given: Obsidian is open on the test vault with the plugin's build from this PR installed, and no modal is open.

prepare.why: eight PK 2267 node types, so the filter panel shows its type search (it appears above seven types) and the chips have names to complete

check.js: (() => { const names = ["PK 2267 Alpha", "PK 2267 Beta", "PK 2267 Gamma", "PK 2267 Delta", "PK 2267 Epsilon", "PK 2267 Zeta", "PK 2267 Eta", "PK 2267 Theta"]; return names.every((name) => proof.obsidian.nodeType(name)); })()

apply.js: (async () => { const plugin = proof.obsidian.plugin(); const settings = plugin.settings; const now = Date.now(); for (const name of ["PK 2267 Alpha", "PK 2267 Beta", "PK 2267 Gamma", "PK 2267 Delta", "PK 2267 Epsilon", "PK 2267 Zeta", "PK 2267 Eta", "PK 2267 Theta"]) { if (settings.nodeTypes.some((type) => type.name === name)) continue; settings.nodeTypes.push({ id: 'pk-2267-' + name.split(' ').pop().toLowerCase(), name, format: name + ' - {content}', created: now, modified: now }); } await plugin.saveSettings(); return true; })()

surface.why: The toolbar row's gap and padding in NodeSearchModal now come from Obsidian size variables, so the input and the two trigger buttons could shift or clip.

surface.area: Node type chips in the search field
surface.why: Chip margin, padding, font size and the Tab-completion hint spacing changed to variables, which could break inline wrapping or the focus outline.

surface.area: Filter and sort trigger buttons (count badge)
surface.why: The badge offset, radius and font size now use variables, so it could clip or misalign against the trigger button.
Row spacing, the Clear filter strip, the type search box and the empty state were all re-spaced, and the borders were forced solid.
Option rows, the Sort by header and the direction toggle use new variables and a forced solid top border.
All sizing now depends on Obsidian's --size-4-*, --font-ui-* and --radius-* variables, so a theme or font-size change, or a missing variable, changes the layout.
